title: Elkik approximation of a generically smooth formal section
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal with $(R,I)$ a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and put $\widehat R=\varprojlim_{m\geq1}R/I^m$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $B$ be a finitely presented commutative $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Assume that the restriction of $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ to $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\setminus V(IB)$ is smooth [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; here $V(IB)$ is the set of prime ideals containing the ideal generated by the image of $I$. For every $R$-algebra homomorphism $\widehat s:B\to\widehat R$ and every integer $N\geq1$, there exists an $R$-algebra homomorphism $s:B\to R$ such that $\pi_N\widehat s=q_Ns$, where $\pi_N:\widehat R\to R/I^N$ is the $N$-th coordinate projection and $q_N:R\to R/I^N$ is the quotient map. No excellence or G-ring hypothesis on $R$ is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.12, printed p.151, special case U=Spec(B) minus V(IB); cited there as Elkik, Chapter II, Theorem 2 bis; read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag is asserted for this result.

proof.text: Prove the stronger assertion for every finitely presented $A$-algebra and every formal section whose punctured image lies in an open $W$ smooth over $A$; no smoothness away from $IA$ on the entire algebra is required. Induct on the number $l$ of chosen generators of $I$, simultaneously for all Noetherian henselian pairs. For $l=0$, $I=0$ and its completion is $A$, so use the formal section itself. For $l=1$ use the principal-ideal approximation lemma with this $W$.

source.place: Elkik II, proof of Theorem 2 bis, printed pp.566–567; agent reconstruction with the indicated existing DAG statements

proof.text: We record the henselian pairs used in the induction. Henselianity forces $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(A)$: otherwise for a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ with $I+\mathfrak m=A$, the distinct idempotents $0,1$ in the finite algebra $A/\mathfrak m$ have the same image in its zero quotient by $I$, contradicting uniqueness. For any $K\subseteq I$, $(A/K,I(A/K))$ is henselian by integral permanence. Also $(A,K)$ is henselian: for a finite $A$-algebra $E$ and an idempotent $e\in E/KE$, reduce it modulo $IE$ and lift to an idempotent $f\in E$ by $(A,I)$. The algebra $E$ is integral, so $IE$ is in its Jacobson radical. In $E/KE$, $e$ and the image of $f$ are equal by uniqueness modulo the radical ideal $IE/KE$; uniqueness of the lift follows the same way. In particular $(A,tA)$ and $(A/t^MA,I(A/t^MA))$ are henselian for every $t\in I$ and $M\geq1$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 09XK (label lemma-integral-over-henselian-pair, line 2753) for quotient permanence, and the idempotent argument of Lemma 0DYD (label lemma-henselian-henselian-pair, line 2765) for the subideal pair, written out here in the finite-algebra form of the definition rather than creating a permanence node

proof.text: For $l>1$ choose $I=(t,a_2,\ldots,a_l)$ and a presentation $B=A[x_1,\ldots,x_d]/J$. The rings $A[x]$ and $B$ are Noetherian, hence the obstruction ideal $H=H_{B/A}$ and its inverse image $\widetilde H\subseteq A[x]$ have finite generating lists. The smooth-locus assertion of ideal calculus identifies $V(H)$ with the nonsmooth locus. The punctured-image hypothesis on $\widehat s$ therefore implies $V(\widehat s(H)\widehat A)\subseteq V(I\widehat A)$. The intersection-of-primes formula implies that each generator of $I\widehat A$ has some power in $\widehat s(H)\widehat A$. If these powers have exponents $e_i\geq1$, every monomial of total degree $h=1+\sum_i(e_i-1)$ contains one of them. Thus $(I\widehat A)^h\subseteq\widehat s(H)\widehat A$.

source.place: Elkik II, proof of Theorem 2 bis, printed pp.566–567; agent reconstruction with the indicated existing DAG statements

proof.text: Put $C=\widehat A_{(t)}$. This ring is Noetherian and $tC$-adically complete. Apply the complete principal obstruction-lifting lemma to the base-changed presentation $C[x]/JC[x]$ and this fixed $h$, obtaining $n_0,r$. Fix $L\geq\max(N,h+1)$ and then $M\geq\max(n_0,r+L,h+1)$. These constants are chosen before taking an approximate point, as required by the lemma's uniform quantifiers. Put $A_0=A/t^MA$ and $I_0=IA_0$. The ring $A_0$ is Noetherian (it is a finite type quotient), is henselian along $I_0$ by Step 2, and $I_0$ defines the same adic topology as $(a_2,\ldots,a_l)A_0$: $t^M=0$, so writing $J_0=(a_2,\ldots,a_l)A_0$, one has $J_0^k\subseteq I_0^k$ and $I_0^k\subseteq J_0^{k-M+1}$ for $k\geq M$ by expanding monomials and discarding those divisible by $t^M$. Thus the powers are cofinal. In particular the induction parameter decreases to at most $l-1$.

source.place: Elkik II, proof of Theorem 2 bis, printed pp.566–567; agent reconstruction with the indicated existing DAG statements

proof.text: Identify $D=\widehat{A_0}_{I_0}$ with $\widehat A_I/t^M\widehat A_I$. Indeed, complete the finite-module exact sequence $0\to t^MA\to A\to A_0\to0$ along $I$. Exactness gives a surjection $\widehat A_I\to D$. The finite-module tensor formula identifies the image of $(t^MA)^\wedge$ with the ideal $t^M\widehat A_I$; the maps on representatives are multiplication and quotient, so this is an isomorphism of rings commuting with every reduction. It follows that $D/I_0^LD$ is canonically $A/(I^L+t^MA)$. As $M\geq L$ and $t\in I$, this last quotient is $A/I^L$. All finite-module hypotheses hold because $A$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Elkik II, proof of Theorem 2 bis, printed pp.566–567; agent reconstruction with the indicated existing DAG statements

proof.text: Reduce $\widehat s$ to a map $B_0=B\otimes_AA_0\to D$. Since $t$ is nilpotent in $A_0$, $V(I_0D)=V(J_0D)$. Its punctured image therefore lies in the base change of the original smooth open $W$, which is smooth by smooth base change (checked on affine opens). Thus the stronger induction assertion, for the ideal generated by $a_2,\ldots,a_l$, supplies a map $s_0:B_0\to A_0$ agreeing with that reduced formal section modulo $I_0^L$. Powers of the two cofinal ideals give the same completion; approximate to a sufficiently high power of $(a_2,\ldots,a_l)$ contained in $I_0^L$. The needed henselianity for this smaller ideal was proved in Step 2. Finite presentation of $B_0$ follows by applying coefficient reduction to the chosen finite equations.

source.place: Elkik II, proof of Theorem 2 bis, printed pp.566–567; agent reconstruction with the indicated existing DAG statements

proof.text: Let $K_0\subseteq A_0$ be generated by evaluation under $s_0$ of the images of $H$. Congruence of polynomial evaluations modulo $I_0^L$, and the power containment in Step 3 reduced to $D$, give $I_0^hD\subseteq K_0D+I_0^LD$. The completion statements show that $D$ is Noetherian and $I_0D$-adically complete. Apply Nakayama to the finite $D$-module $(I_0^hD+K_0D)/K_0D$: since $L\geq h+1$, it equals its product with $I_0D$. This ideal is in the Jacobson radical because $D$ is adically complete. Hence $I_0^hD\subseteq K_0D$. The map $A_0\to D$ is faithfully flat, since $I_0\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(A_0)$ by Step 2. Ideal contraction now gives $I_0^h\subseteq K_0$ in $A_0$, in particular $t^h\bmod t^M\in K_0$. This is containment for the images of the original $H$, not merely for a possibly larger obstruction ideal after base change.

source.place: Elkik II, proof of Theorem 2 bis, printed pp.566–567; agent reconstruction with the indicated existing DAG statements

proof.text: Lift the generator values of $s_0$ arbitrarily to a tuple $a\in C^d$, using $C/t^MC=A/t^MA$. Then $f(a)\in t^MC$ for every $f\in J$. Write $K_C(a)$ for evaluation of the inverse image of $H_{B_C/C}$ in $C[x]$. Ideal calculus gives $H_{B/A}B_C\subseteq H_{B_C/C}$. Consequently Step 7 yields $t^h\in K_C(a)+t^MC$. Apply Nakayama to $((t^h)+K_C(a))/K_C(a)$, using $M>h$ and $tC\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(C)$, to remove the error $t^M$ and obtain $t^h\in K_C(a)$. The complete lifting lemma at $n=M$ now gives $b\in C^d$ solving every relation and congruent to $a$ modulo $t^{M-r}$. It defines an $A$-algebra map $u:B\to C$.

source.place: Elkik II, proof of Theorem 2 bis, printed pp.566–567; agent reconstruction with the indicated existing DAG statements

proof.text: The new section $u$ meets the original smooth locus away from $t$. To see this using precisely the needed ideal, let $K_b$ be generated in $C$ by evaluations at $b$ of polynomial lifts of the original $H$. Their evaluations at $a$ agree modulo $t^{M-r}$. Step 7 and $M-r\geq L>h$ imply $t^h\in K_b+t^{M-r}C$. Nakayama on $((t^h)+K_b)/K_b$ gives $t^h\in K_b$. Every prime of $C$ avoiding $t$ thus avoids at least one image of $H$, so its image in $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is in $W_1=\operatorname{Spec}B\setminus V(H)$. Ideal calculus identifies this open as the smooth locus. By $(A,tA)$ henselian from Step 2, apply principal-ideal approximation with the smooth open $W_1$ to obtain $s:B\to A$ agreeing with $u$ modulo $t^L$.

source.place: Elkik II, proof of Theorem 2 bis, printed pp.566–567; agent reconstruction with the indicated existing DAG statements

proof.text: Compare the maps in $\widehat A_I$. There is a canonical map $C\to\widehat A_I$: its $k$-th coordinate is $C\to A/t^kA\to A/I^k$; these maps are compatible because $t^kA\subseteq I^k$. The element $b_i$ and the value $s_0(x_i)$ agree modulo $t^{M-r}$, hence agree modulo $I^L$ under the quotient identification of Step 5. The latter agrees with $\widehat s(x_i)$ modulo $I^L$ by Step 6. Finally $s(x_i)$ agrees with $b_i$ modulo $t^L\subseteq I^L$. Thus $q_Ls=\pi_L\widehat s$ on generators and on $A$, hence on $B$. Reducing to order $N\leq L$ gives the claimed equality. This completes the induction for the stronger assertion. For the item take $W=\operatorname{Spec}B\setminus V(IB)$: the punctured-image condition is automatic for an $A$-algebra map, since inverse image of $V(IB)$ is $V(I\widehat A)$.
